question: Rahul borrowed a sum of money at simple interest of 5% per annum for the first 3 years, 7% per annum for the next 5 years, and 9% per annum for the period beyond 8 years. If he pays a total of ₹6800 as interest only at the end of 10 years, how much money did he borrow?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total effective interest rate = (3 × 5%) + (5 × 7%) + (2 × 9%)

⇒ Total rate = 15% + 35% + 18% = 68%

We are given that 68% of the total Principal = ₹6800

⇒ Principal (100%) = (6800 ÷ 68) × 100 = ₹10000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Total Time = 10 Years

 Total Interest = 15% + 35% + 18% = 68%
 68% = ₹6800 → 100% = ₹10000

**Given:**

Rate for the first 3 years (R₁) = 5% per annum

Rate for the next 5 years (R₂) = 7% per annum

Total time given = 10 years, so remaining time (T₃) = 10 − (3 + 5) = 2 years

Rate for the remaining 2 years (R₃) = 9% per annum

Total Simple Interest (SI) paid at the end = ₹6800

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total SI = SI₁ + SI₂ + SI₃

⇒ 6800 = (P × 5 × 3) ÷ 100 + (P × 7 × 5) ÷ 100 + (P × 9 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ 6800 = (15P ÷ 100) + (35P ÷ 100) + (18P ÷ 100)

⇒ 6800 = (15P + 35P + 18P) ÷ 100

⇒ 6800 = 68P ÷ 100

⇒ P = (6800 × 100) ÷ 68

⇒ P = 10000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹10000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effective Rate of Simple Interest

When money is borrowed at different rates for different periods, the total effective percentage interest is simply the sum of the products of each rate and its respective time period: Rₑffₑ꜀ₜᵢvₑ = R₁T₁ + R₂T₂ + ...

Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount to be repaid at the end of the term is the sum of the Principal and the Simple Interest generated: A = P + SI = P(1 + RT ÷ 100).

Difference Between SI and CI

Unlike Compound Interest where interest is calculated on the accumulated interest at the end of each cycle, Simple Interest is always calculated solely on the initial Principal amount for the entire duration.
